subline: Plumbing · Portland metro (Willamette Valley) · GA4 property 100200300
pulse: We generated 279 leads for you (163 tracking-line calls, 103 site call-clicks, 13 forms), essentially flat vs. 278. The bigger story is what happened after: tracked job value jumped 105% to $314,748, because the average job size nearly doubled. Same number of leads, much bigger jobs.

callout.k: Half the leads have no traceable source
callout.body: 163 of the 279 leads come in through the call-tracking line with no marketing source attached, so GA4 can’t yet tell us which ad, search, or listing drove them, or which channel is behind the jump in job value. Pulling the source detail from the call-tracking / job system will close that gap.

left_chart.title: Weekly leads · last 13 weeks
left_chart.caption: Climbed into mid-July (peak 89, week of Jul 13), eased into the 60s since, still well above where it started.

right_chart.title: Leads by channel (traceable) · last 28 days
right_chart.caption: Google Ads is the strongest traceable channel (~1.5× site average). Plus 163 tracking-line calls with no source.

flags.text: Job value up 105%. Average job nearly doubled ($1,010 → $1,897) on flat lead volume, bigger jobs at the same lead count.
Google Ads is the best traceable channel, converting ~1.5× the site average, with room to grow without losing quality.
Two quiet spots: Layton sent 37 visits and 0 leads; a “toilet drains by itself” blog post drew 144 visits and 0 leads.
